evidence_items.publisher: Zheng et al., ByteDance and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Sections 3.1–3.2, Overall Performance and Analysis and Insights
evidence_items.explanation: The study evaluates legacy GPT-3 models and GPT-4 under aligned settings across more than twenty benchmarks and seven capability categories. Its overall analysis reports broad improvements across those categories from GPT-3 to GPT-4.

OpenAI's comparison finds strong preferences for o1-preview on reasoning-heavy tasks but exceptions on natural-language tasks. This directly supports the claimed unevenness, while the same publication documents substantial reasoning gains.

Independent testing found improvements on an abstract-reasoning benchmark as well. This limits any reading that o1's benefits were confined to the particular math and coding examples, but does not establish uniform gains.

unresolved_gaps: The two generation comparisons were not evaluated on one identical, representative task distribution.
No numerical measure of uniformity was supplied by Marcus.
